amendments.body: The patch does not implement the bead it is supposed to close. The only new coverage is a nitrification/alkalinity suite in crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1, and the runtime changes are limited to alkalinity bookkeeping/tracing around the nitrogen cycle in crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229, crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12, and crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131. None of the requested shrimp scenario tests, the 1000+ hour breeding run, the per-tick shrimp/water trace dumps, or the e2e summary runner/report are present, so the acceptance criteria for tanksim-6e5.6.6 are still unmet.
amendments.rationale: This is a scope/correctness miss against the task itself: merging it would leave the requested shrimp regression coverage absent while appearing to complete the bead.

amendments.body: The new alkalinity diagnostics still print the wrong unit in the detailed failure paths. assert_budget_balanced switches the headline to meq, but the per-system lines are still hard-coded to mg at crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:474, and assert_per_tick_balanced still hard-codes mg at crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:496 and crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:502. If an alkalinity assertion fails, the report will mix meq and mg in the same message and mislead anyone trying to calibrate or debug the failure.
amendments.rationale: These helpers are supposed to explain budget failures. Incorrect units are a real debugging hazard for the new alkalinity work, not a cosmetic issue.

payload.summary: Read the changed implementation and tests end-to-end and ran targeted tank_core tests; the code compiles and the targeted suites pass, but I found two blockers: the patch is solving nitrification-alkalinity work instead of the requested shrimp-scenario deliverable, and the new alkalinity failure diagnostics still report the wrong units.
